newsitem.title: CHINA: HK's Tung attends Beijing finale of handover panel.
newsitem.headline: HK's Tung attends Beijing finale of handover panel.

text.p: Hong Kong's new leader Tung Chee-hwa left for Beijing on Friday for a key meeting to shut down one of the groups that steered the former British colony into Chinese rule.

"He's going up there as a deputy director of the Preparatory Committee and to wind it up because this is the last session," a Tung spokesman said. It is Tung's first visit to the capital since Hong Kong's July 1 handover to China.

Under Beijing's close guidance, the 150-member committee of Chinese officials and Hong Kong worthies crafted the new power structures that have replaced the 156-year-old British colonial administration.
The committee has been chaired by China's Foreign Minister Qian Qichen, and Tung was one of nine vice-chairmen.
Tung, appointed by China to govern Hong Kong after the British departed 10 days ago, will return to Hong Kong on Saturday.
